board: Texas State Board of Public Accountancy (TSBPA)

cycle.note: Licenses renew every year on the last day of your birth month. Each renewal looks back 36 months (120 hours) and 12 months (20 hours). No carryover.
cycle.label: Last 36 months

requirements.label: Technical
requirements.note: At least half of the required credits must be technical, because no more than half can be non-technical (§ 523.118(a)). Technical: accounting, attest, tax, consulting, economics, finance, IT, regulatory ethics.

requirements.label: Non-technical
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than half of the required credits can be non-technical (§ 523.118(a)): communications, computer software and applications, behavioral ethics, business management and organization.

requirements.label: Nano-learning
requirements.note: Maximum, not a target. No more than half of the required credits can come from nano-learning (§ 523.118(b)). We use each course's delivery format — set it to Nano Learning for nano courses.

requirements.label: Board-approved Texas ethics course
requirements.note: A 4-hour TSBPA-approved ethics course every two years. We count courses with "Texas" and "ethics" (or "TSBPA") in the title — edit the title if yours isn't picked up. Out-of-state licensees with no Texas clients may meet their home state's ethics rule instead.

newLicensee.note: Texas phases CPE in over your first years of licensure (Rule 523.112).

phaseIn.note: No CPE is required for your first partial license period or your first full 12-month license period.
Second full license year: 20 hours in the 12 months before renewal.
Third full license year: 60 hours in the 24 months before renewal, at least 20 in the last 12.
Fourth full license year: 100 hours in the 36 months before renewal, at least 20 in the last 12.

licenseDateHint: Texas licenses renew every year on the last day of your birth month.
issueDateHint: Needed if you were licensed in the last four years — Texas phases CPE in for new licensees.
limitsNotTracked: Nano-learning: max 50% of required hours in three years.
Certification programs (CFP, CIA, CFE…): max 50% in three years.
Instruction credit: max 20 hours a year.
toVerify: Business Law, Statistics and Specialized Knowledge treated as technical, and Personal Development, Personnel/HR and Production as non-technical — the rule lists examples, not every NASBA field.
Non-technical cap during the phase-in years: we apply 50% of that year's required total (e.g. 30 of 60).
Not tracked: certification programs (CFP, CIA, CFE, securities licenses) capped at 50% of required credits (§ 523.118(c)).
Non-residents may follow their principal-place-of-business state's CPE rules instead (§ 523.112(e)); the app always applies Texas rules.
